# Sirach Chapter 47 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 47 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## Council Notes

Sirach 47 is structured around David (vv. 1–11) and Solomon (vv. 12–25). The David section is primarily praise; the Solomon section divides into praise for his wisdom (vv. 12–17) and blame for his sin (vv. 19–21). The chapter ends in darkness with the divided kingdom. Ben Sira never loses sight of the historical consequences of Solomon's failures.

**Key decisions:**
- v. 2: The simile comparing David to separated fat is striking and must not be smoothed. Fat was the choicest portion offered to God.
- v. 6: "daughters of Israel" (EMET literal) vs. "women of Israel" (LOGOS/PNEUMA) — Greek thugateres Israēl could be either. "Women" is more accurate in this context (1 Sam. 18:6–7 reference).
- v. 8: "set his hands right" — the gesture of properly orienting oneself before God. EMET/LOGOS preserve the idiom.
- v. 9: "from their sound he made sweet melody" (EMET) vs. "with their voices made sweet melody" (LOGOS) — the Greek is ambiguous; SOPHIA adopts the LOGOS reading.
- v. 11: "took away his sins" (EMET) vs. "forgave his sins" (LOGOS) — Greek apheilato = removed, took away. EMET is more literal.
- v. 19: "put your loins beside women" (EMET) — literal rendering of the idiom for sexual relations. LOGOS and PNEUMA soften; SOPHIA adopts a middle path.
- v. 22: "a root from himself" — the Davidic root/shoot imagery important for messianic reading; preserve "root."

---

**47:1** After him Nathan rose up to prophesy in the days of David.

**47:2** As the fat is separated from the peace offering, so David was set apart from among the children of Israel.

**47:3** He played with lions as with young goats, and with bears as with lambs of the flock.

**47:4** In his youth, did he not slay a giant and remove reproach from the people, when he lifted his hand with a smooth stone and brought down the boasting of Goliath?

**47:5** For he called upon the Most High Lord, who gave strength to his right arm to strike down a mighty warrior and raise high the horn of his people.

**47:6** So the women of Israel acclaimed him for his tens of thousands and sang his praises.

**47:7** When he took up his armor and went to war, he drew the sword against the Philistines, and his hand made short work of many.

**47:8** Before any undertaking, he would set his hands aright and give thanks to the Holy One, the Most High, with words of glory.

**47:9** With his whole heart he sang praises and loved his Maker. He placed singers before the altar, and from their voices he drew sweet melody.

**47:10** He gave beauty to the feast days and arranged the appointed seasons in order throughout the year, while they praised his holy name and the sanctuary resounded from morning.

**47:11** The Lord took away his sins and exalted his horn forever; he gave him a covenant of kings and a throne of glory in Israel.

**47:12** After him rose a wise son who lived in safety because of him.

**47:13** Solomon reigned in days of peace, and God gave him rest on every side, so that he might build a house for his name and prepare a sanctuary to endure forever.

**47:14** How wise you were in your youth! You were filled with understanding like a flooding river!

**47:15** Your mind covered the earth, and you filled it with dark parables.

**47:16** Your name reached to far-off islands, and you were loved for your peace.

**47:17** For your songs and proverbs and parables and interpretations, the lands marveled at you.

**47:18** In the name of the Lord God, who is called the God of Israel, you gathered gold like tin and amassed silver like lead.

**47:19** But you laid yourself open to women, and by your body you were brought into subjection.

**47:20** You put a stain upon your honor and profaned your descendants, bringing wrath upon your children — and they were grieved because of your folly,

**47:21** so that the kingdom was divided, and out of Ephraim a rebel kingdom arose.

**47:22** But the Lord will not abandon his mercy, nor let any of his words fail; he will not blot out the posterity of his chosen one, nor destroy the line of him who loved him; so he gave a remnant to Jacob and to David a root from his own stock.

**47:23** Solomon rested with his ancestors and left behind one of his seed — Rehoboam, broad in folly and lacking in sense — who made the people turn away by his counsel. And Jeroboam son of Nebat led Israel into sin and set Ephraim on the path of transgression.

**47:24** Their sins multiplied enormously, so that they were driven from their land.

**47:25** For they sought out every kind of wickedness, until vengeance came upon them.
